question: Using Bohr’s model, show that the radius of the permitted orbit increases as $n^2$ and the energy becomes less negative as $n$ increases. Hence compare the radius and energy of the first and third orbits of hydrogen atom.

options.B: $r_n\propto n$ and energy becomes more negative as $n$ increases; hence $r_3=3r_1$ and $E_3=-40.8\text{ eV}$.
options.C: For hydrogen, $r_n=r_1n^2$ and $E_n=-\dfrac{13.6}{n^2}\text{ eV}$. Thus $r_3=9r_1$, while $E_1=-13.6\text{ eV}$ and $E_3=-\dfrac{13.6}{9}\text{ eV}\approx-1.51\text{ eV}$. The higher orbit is larger and the electron is less tightly bound.
options.D: All permitted Bohr orbits have equal radius and equal energy.
